lines.before: The methodology kit is the baseline every project starts from. These rules keep it current, small and enforced. Each is checked by a machine where one can check it; the check is named.
lines.after: The methodology kit is the baseline every project starts from. These rules keep it current, small and enforced. Each is checked by a machine where one can check it; the check is named. Text the owner wrote or approved word for word (Hard Rule 14 among it) stays word for word, and only the owner edits it; Hard Rule 14 is pinned by a test, and other owner text gets its pin when it is touched.

lines.before: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **Two passes:** one large sweep, then ONE short re-sweep over the whole batch (by tier: rule:sweep-tiers; never per fix - an undamped loop) of whether the fixes broke anything; a third only for a major re-sweep finding. A finding carries to the next run only at medium or below: a high or critical is fixed before the PR (found after it: on the open PR), or the owner accepts it.
lines.after: **Hard rules:** batch at G3 (triage and diagnose everything, then fix roots). **One sweep:** one large sweep per branch; every fix ships with a test that fails before it, guard and permission fixes too; CI runs the full suite and auto-fix handles red. A second pass is the owner's call; escapes are measured next build. A finding carries to the next run only at medium or below: a high or critical is fixed before the PR (found after it: on the open PR), or the owner accepts it.

lines.before: 4. **A run's order:** the feature comes FIRST (a fix first only when high or critical): the confirmed work order's next, else the owner's pick; leftovers and recorded carry-overs ride on its branch (unless large, risky, device-only or a design call); ONE large sweep after both, the short re-sweep, one PR. The Resume Point names the feature pick first.
lines.after: 4. **A run's order:** the feature comes FIRST (a fix first only when high or critical): the confirmed work order's next, else the owner's pick; leftovers and recorded carry-overs ride on its branch (unless large, risky, device-only or a design call); ONE large sweep after both, CI, one PR. The Resume Point names the feature pick first.

lines.before: **Done iff** a report exists at `<sweep folder>/YYYY-MM-DD-<milestone>.md` with date, milestone, branch / commit; each dimension PASS or with findings; every high / critical `FIXED <commit>` or `ACCEPTED owner <why>`; for the deep tier, "still aligned with the version goals? YES/NO + evidence". <!-- PROJECT ADAPTER A22 -->
lines.after: **Done iff** a report exists at `<sweep folder>/YYYY-MM-DD-<milestone>.md` with date, milestone, branch / commit; each dimension PASS or with findings; every high / critical `FIXED <commit>` or `ACCEPTED owner <why>` (the owner then merges); for the deep tier, "still aligned with the version goals? YES/NO + evidence". <!-- PROJECT ADAPTER A22 -->

lines.before: **Re-sweep by tier:** feature, first push and launch gate run the one short re-sweep (rule:finding-pipeline); a fix tier's fix check covers it; triage runs none unless it found something. A stated exemption is left only for a PR that changes no code and no public text. **How: the pre-pr-sweep skill.**
lines.after: **After the sweep:** each fix carries its failing-first test and CI runs the full suite (rule:finding-pipeline); a fix tier keeps its fix check. A stated exemption is left only for a PR that changes no code and no public text. **How: the pre-pr-sweep skill.**

lines.before: **Pipeline:** `build -> all gates green -> Parking Lot triage -> Pre-PR Deep Sweep -> fixes + re-sweep -> gate -> Pre-Push Op-Test -> fixes + gate -> PR body (carrying the sweep summary) + audit to the owner -> push + PR (owner) -> preview test -> merge (owner) -> Post-Merge Check -> release (owner's go)`. Why: a "now" idea is built and swept inside the same PR.
lines.after: **Pipeline:** `build -> all gates green -> Parking Lot triage -> Pre-PR Deep Sweep -> test-first fixes -> gate -> Pre-Push Op-Test -> fixes + gate -> PR body (carrying the sweep summary) + audit to the owner -> push + PR (owner) -> preview test -> merge (owner) -> Post-Merge Check -> release (owner's go)`. Why: a "now" idea is built and swept inside the same PR.

lines.before: - **Full gate:** once per phase end and before every PR; independent steps run side by side, every step still runs; a fix after an Op-Test re-runs only the touched suites, the PR's final gate covers the rest; E2E may run beside the non-building steps (after type-check sync), never beside a build (shared folders and servers). **Size budgets:** once per batch; bisect only when a line is over.
lines.after: - **Full gate:** once per phase end and before every PR (where CI runs the full suite, as in the kit, CI is that run); independent steps run side by side, every step still runs; a fix after an Op-Test re-runs only the touched suites, the PR's final gate covers the rest; E2E may run beside the non-building steps (after type-check sync), never beside a build (shared folders and servers). **Size budgets:** once per batch; bisect only when a line is over.

lines.before: - **Team mode:** batch (the main session leads) under about 5 units, orchestrated above. **One review lead** runs the whole tail (sweep, fixes, fix check, re-sweep, op-test, design calls) with one stop.
lines.after: - **Team mode:** batch (the main session leads) under about 5 units, orchestrated above. **One review lead** runs the whole tail (sweep, fixes, fix check, op-test, design calls) with one stop.

lines.before: - **Fix sets:** one checker may do the fix check and the re-sweep together only when the fixes cover at most 2 roots, none above low; otherwise run both. Why: the separate re-sweep catches half-done fixes.
lines.after: - **Fix sets:** the fix check confirms each fix's test fails on the code before it. Why: with no re-sweep, the failing-first test is what catches a half-done fix.
